label: late original-phase steps (t>=5) of sequences starting with t
explanation: Sparse feature (~0.05% of steps). 85% of activation mass is in sequences whose first original token is t (24x lift); fires only during the late original phase, at t=5-8 (peak t=6), with a small tail on the <DEL> step; never in the copy phase or at t<4. The predicate gets ~80% of mass but low precision (~9%): most late original-phase steps of t-initial sequences stay silent. Magnitude goes up when the current input is the digit 0 (9x lift, 35% of mass; top examples are 0 inputs), when the second token is v (t v ... prefixes dominate the top examples), and with prior inputs like b/o/m/w. Adding these content conditions raises precision only to 13-52% and costs a lot of recall, so the token-content dependence is not fully captured. Rare weak firing on non-t-initial sequences (often with t or v at position 1).
